answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before it may trade, like a juniper planted at the inlet of a market: the deposit is a cipher the agent must solve fresh for every new identity, tying each account to a real, scarce cost. A single operator spinning up thousands of fake agents would have to fund every stake and wait out every lock, so cheap mass identities stop paying for themselves while honest agents recover their deposit by behaving well.
